literature_notes: ANPEP (Aminopeptidase N) is a type II single-pass transmembrane protein with a short intracellular N-terminus (residues 1-9), a TM helix (10-32), and a large extracellular ectodomain (33-967). Both ledger lines (L1, L2) describe pEGFP-C1-APN fusion constructs in which EGFP is placed at the N-terminus of the full-length APN protein by the pEGFP-C1 vector architecture. Because APN's N-terminus (residues 1-9) is intracellular, the EGFP tag in these constructs is on the cytoplasmic face — not the extracellular surface. These constructs therefore do not qualify as extracellular surface tag insertions. L2 also mentions Fc-domain fusions of the soluble ectodomain, which are explicitly excluded by the rules (soluble ectodomain / Fc-fusion reagent). No ledger line supports an insertion on the extracellular face of ANPEP; zero sites are reported.

literature_other_positions.note: pEGFP-C1-APN constructs place EGFP N-terminal to full-length APN; because APN residues 1-9 are intracellular, the EGFP tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.

Same pEGFP-C1 N-terminal fusion architecture applied to 17 animal APN orthologs; EGFP is on the intracellular face. The Fc-ectodomain fusions also described are excluded as soluble Fc-fusion reagents.
